title: Where do four moves on a line with only zero land?
description: Four sums and take aways are worked on a line with only zero marked. Adding a negative number moves left, and taking away a negative number is a walk to the right. Keeko's doubt is that taking away a negative number moves left.
teaching_notes: One idea: on a line with only zero marked, adding a negative number moves left and taking away a negative number moves right. Watch for students who think every minus sign sends the walker to the left.

source: Use unmarked number lines to evaluate these expressions: a. -125 + (-30)  b. +105 - (-55)  c. +80 - (-150)  d. -99 - (-200)
video_script.why: The child works four sums and take aways on lines with only zero marked, and sees that taking away a negative number moves right.
video_script.substitution: The four expressions of the book question, each drawn on a line with only zero marked.
video_script.anchor: the line of the book with only zero marked, with each walk drawn as an arrow
video_script.wrong_answer: taking away negative fifty five moves us left
video_script.wrong_move: believes every minus sign sends the walker to the left, so taking away a negative number makes the answer smaller
video_script.payoff_line: Taking away a negative number moves us to the right.

final_answer.spoken: negative one hundred fifty five, one hundred sixty, two hundred thirty and one hundred one

maths_rules: a sum: start at the first number, a negative second number moves left
a take away x - y is the movement from y to x (target - start)
slip: a take away of a negative number is a walk to the right, so the answer is bigger than the first number
video_script.design: Four lines with only zero marked, one per expression; each walk is an arrow, and a check line adds the movement to its start.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a line with only 0 marked; the four expressions in a list

marks.scene: the title card arrives and a line with only 0 marked is drawn
marks.ask: four expressions slide in as a list

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a line with only zero marked.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Four sums and take aways are given.
<bookmark mark='look'/>In the second one, we take away a negative number. Does the walker go left or right?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Target number - Starting number = Movement; + negative moves left

marks.sum: an arrow to the left is marked adding a negative number
marks.rule: the line Target number - Starting number = Movement is written

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Adding a negative number moves us to the left.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>A take away is the movement from the second number to the first.

marks.given: the four expressions are written in a list

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one sum and three take aways.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each

marks.find: the words value of each are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find where each walk ends.

beats.on_screen: a. -125 + (-30): mark -125, then an arrow of 30 steps left = -155

marks.a: -125 is marked left of 0 and an arrow of 30 steps runs further left to -155

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, negative one hundred twenty five plus negative thirty. Mark the start, then walk thirty steps to the left, to negative one hundred fifty five.

marks.b2: an arrow runs from -55 to 0 and on to 105, and +160 is written
marks.c2: an arrow runs from -150 to 0 and on to 80, and +230 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='b'/>Step two, one hundred five take away negative fifty five.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>That is the walk from negative fifty five to one hundred five.
Fifty five to zero, and one hundred five more, is one hundred sixty to the right.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Eighty take away negative one hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>That is the walk from negative one hundred fifty to eighty.
It is two hundred thirty to the right.

marks.d2: an arrow runs right from -200 to -99 and +101 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d'/>Step three, negative ninety nine take away negative two hundred.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>That is the walk from negative two hundred to negative ninety nine.
It is two hundred take away ninety nine, which is one hundred one to the right.

beats.on_screen: Check: starting number + movement = target number;  -55 + 160 = 105;  -150 + 230 = 80;  -200 + 101 = -99

marks.check: the check line starting number plus movement equals target number is written

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by adding the movement to the starting number.
<bookmark mark='bc'/>Negative fifty five plus one hundred sixty is one hundred five.
Negative one hundred fifty plus two hundred thirty is eighty.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Negative two hundred plus one hundred one is negative ninety nine.

marks.pay: the three arrows to the right glow

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The answers are negative one hundred fifty five, one hundred sixty, two hundred thirty and one hundred one.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Taking away a negative number moves us to the right.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: an arrow left from 105 ending at 50 struck out; the arrow from -55 to 105 lights up

marks.doubt: an arrow runs left from 105 to 50
marks.fix: the arrow is struck out and the arrow from -55 to 105 lights up
marks.why: the walker is seen to climb from below zero up to 105

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks taking away negative fifty five moves us left, because there is a take away.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the walk starts at negative fifty five, and it must reach one hundred five.
<bookmark mark='why'/>That is a climb to the right, so the answer is bigger than one hundred five.
